result_summary: Adaptive intrinsic tracking is not universally superior to strong full-space least squares. Tuned full-space RLS clearly wins at N=20,k=3 with T=3200, while intrinsic tracking remains clearly better at N=50 and above; at lower sample budgets intrinsic tracking wins more broadly. Generic PAST-style tracking largely matches Oja and can outperform it in the hardest short-budget/high-N cell, so the supported mechanism is adaptive low-dimensional tracking/conditioning rather than Oja specifically.
